syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

book.title: Physics Part-II
book.edition: NCERT (reprint year not stated in the prelims)

topics.title: Reflection of light by spherical mirrors

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the Cartesian sign convention to distances and heights for mirrors and lenses.
Relate the focal length of a spherical mirror to its radius of curvature for paraxial rays.
Use the mirror equation and magnification to locate and describe images formed by spherical mirrors.

topics.title: Refraction of light

concepts.learning_objective: Apply Snell's law and the properties of relative refractive index to the bending of light.
Explain lateral shift in a glass slab and calculate the apparent depth of an object under a liquid.

topics.title: Total internal reflection and its applications

concepts.learning_objective: State the conditions for total internal reflection and relate the critical angle to refractive index.
Explain how totally reflecting prisms and optical fibres use total internal reflection.

topics.title: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses

concepts.learning_objective: Use the relation for refraction at a single spherical surface between two media.
Use the lens maker's formula to relate focal length to radii of curvature and refractive index.
Apply the thin lens formula and magnification to locate and describe images formed by lenses.

topics.title: Power of a lens and combination of thin lenses

concepts.learning_objective: Define the power of a lens in dioptres and relate its sign to the type of lens.
Find the effective power, focal length and magnification of thin lenses in contact.

topics.title: Refraction through a prism

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the angle of deviation of a prism to the angles of incidence, emergence and the prism angle.
Use the minimum deviation condition to find the refractive index of a prism, including a thin prism.

topics.title: Optical instruments: the microscope

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a simple microscope magnifies and calculate its magnifying power.
Describe image formation in a compound microscope and calculate its magnifying power.

topics.title: Optical instruments: the telescope

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the magnifying power and tube length of a refracting telescope in normal adjustment.
Evaluate how objective size and mirror objectives improve light gathering, resolution and image quality.

topics.title: Introduction: corpuscular and wave models of light

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the predictions of the corpuscular and wave models of light for refraction and identify which experiment settled the question.
Explain how Maxwell's electromagnetic theory resolved the difficulty of light travelling through vacuum.

topics.title: Huygens principle and wavefronts

concepts.learning_objective: Define a wavefront and identify spherical and plane wavefronts and their relation to rays.
Use Huygens' construction of secondary wavelets to find the position of a wavefront at a later time.

topics.title: Refraction and reflection of plane waves using Huygens principle

concepts.learning_objective: Derive Snell's law and the law of reflection using Huygens' construction.
Explain why frequency stays constant while speed and wavelength change on refraction.
Describe how wavefronts change on passing through prisms and lenses and on reflection from mirrors.

topics.title: Coherent and incoherent addition of waves

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish coherent and incoherent sources and the resulting intensity patterns.
State the path and phase difference conditions for constructive and destructive interference.
Apply I = 4 I0 cos^2(phi/2) to find the intensity at a point in an interference pattern.

topics.title: Interference of light waves and Young's experiment

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Young's arrangement produces two coherent sources from a single source.
Calculate positions of bright and dark fringes and the fringe width in Young's double-slit experiment.

topics.title: Diffraction at a single slit

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the single-slit diffraction pattern and locate its minima at angles n(lambda)/a.
Compare interference and diffraction and relate the double-slit pattern to both.

topics.title: Polarisation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain polarisation as a property of transverse waves and describe linearly polarised and unpolarised light.
Apply Malus' law to find the intensity of light transmitted through combinations of polaroids.

chapters.title: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

topics.title: Electron emission and the work function

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the measurements of e/m by Thomson and of e by Millikan established the electron as a universal particle of known mass.
Define the work function of a metal and use the electron volt as a unit of energy.
Distinguish thermionic, field and photoelectric emission by the way energy is supplied to free electrons.

topics.title: Discovery of the photoelectric effect

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the observations of Hertz, Hallwachs and Lenard that revealed photoelectric emission.
Explain why different metals need light above different threshold frequencies to emit electrons.

topics.title: Experimental study of the photoelectric effect

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the photocurrent and the saturation current to the intensity of the incident light.
Define the stopping potential and relate it to the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons.
Interpret photocurrent versus collector potential curves for light of different frequencies.

topics.title: Photoelectric effect and the wave theory of light

concepts.learning_objective: State what the classical wave picture of light predicts for photoelectric emission.
Explain which observations of the photoelectric effect the wave picture fails to explain and why.

topics.title: Einstein's photoelectric equation

concepts.learning_objective: Apply Einstein's equation Kmax = h nu - phi0 to calculate kinetic energies and stopping potentials.
Calculate the threshold frequency of a metal from its work function using nu0 = phi0/h.
Interpret the straight-line graph of stopping potential against frequency to obtain h/e and the threshold frequency.

topics.title: Particle nature of light: the photon

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the energy and momentum of a photon and the photon flux of a monochromatic source.
State the properties of photons, including their neutrality and behaviour in collisions.

topics.title: Wave nature of matter

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the de Broglie relation lambda = h/p to material particles and photons.
Explain why matter waves are significant for sub-atomic particles but not for everyday objects.

topics.title: Early ideas: Thomson's model and line spectra

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Thomson's plum pudding model and compare it with Rutherford's nuclear model.
Distinguish the continuous spectrum of dense matter from the line spectrum of a rarefied gas.

topics.title: Alpha-particle scattering and Rutherford's nuclear model

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the observations of the Geiger-Marsden experiment and the assumptions used to analyse them.
Relate the impact parameter of an alpha particle to its angle of scattering.
Calculate the distance of closest approach of an alpha particle using energy conservation.

topics.title: Electron orbits in Rutherford's model

concepts.learning_objective: Use the balance of electrostatic and centripetal force to relate orbit radius and electron speed.
Relate the kinetic, potential and total energy of an orbiting electron and interpret the negative total energy.

topics.title: Atomic spectra

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why an emission line spectrum acts as a fingerprint of an element.
Explain how an absorption spectrum forms and how it relates to the emission spectrum of the same gas.

topics.title: Bohr model of the hydrogen atom and energy levels

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why classical electromagnetic theory predicts that Rutherford's atom is unstable.
State Bohr's three postulates, including the quantisation of angular momentum.
Use E = -13.6/n^2 eV to find excitation and ionisation energies of hydrogen.

topics.title: The line spectra of the hydrogen atom

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the frequency or wavelength of the photon emitted in a transition between two levels.
Decide which photons a hydrogen atom can absorb from the energy gaps between its levels.

topics.title: de Broglie's explanation of Bohr's second postulate and limitations of the model

concepts.learning_objective: Explain quantised orbits as circular standing de Broglie waves with 2 pi r = n lambda.
State the limitations of Bohr's model for multi-electron atoms and line intensities.

topics.title: Atomic masses and composition of the nucleus

concepts.learning_objective: Define the atomic mass unit and calculate the average atomic mass of an element from its isotopic abundances.
Describe the nucleus in terms of Z, N and A and explain how the neutron was discovered.
Classify nuclides as isotopes, isobars or isotones from their Z, N and A.

topics.title: Size of the nucleus

concepts.learning_objective: Use R = R0 A^(1/3) to find and compare nuclear radii.
Explain why nuclear density is independent of mass number and compare it with ordinary matter.

topics.title: Mass-energy and nuclear binding energy

concepts.learning_objective: Apply E = mc^2 and the relation 1 u = 931.5 MeV/c^2.
Calculate mass defect, binding energy and binding energy per nucleon of a nucleus.
Interpret the binding energy per nucleon curve to compare the stability of nuclei.

topics.title: Nuclear force

concepts.learning_objective: State the properties of the nuclear force: strong, short-ranged and charge independent.
Interpret the potential energy curve of a pair of nucleons as a function of separation.

topics.title: Radioactivity

concepts.learning_objective: Recall Becquerel's discovery of radioactivity and that it is a nuclear phenomenon.
Identify alpha, beta and gamma decay and the changes they produce in a nucleus.

topics.title: Nuclear energy and fission

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the energy released in nuclear and chemical processes and explain mass-energy interconversion in both.
Balance fission reactions and estimate the energy released in fission.

topics.title: Nuclear fusion in stars and controlled fusion

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why fusion needs very high temperatures to overcome the Coulomb barrier.
Describe the proton-proton cycle by which hydrogen fuses into helium in the sun.
State the main challenge of controlled thermonuclear fusion in a reactor.

chapters.title: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits

topics.title: Classification of metals, insulators and semiconductors

concepts.learning_objective: Classify solids as metals, semiconductors or insulators from their resistivity and conductivity.
Use the energy band gap between valence and conduction bands to explain conduction in metals, insulators and semiconductors.

topics.title: Intrinsic semiconductors

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the thermal generation of electron-hole pairs in pure Si and Ge and the relation ne = nh = ni.
Describe the apparent motion of holes and the total current as the sum of electron and hole currents.

topics.title: Extrinsic semiconductors: n-type and p-type

concepts.learning_objective: Identify donor and acceptor dopants and the majority and minority carriers in n-type and p-type semiconductors.
Apply ne nh = ni^2 to find carrier concentrations in a doped semiconductor.
Locate donor and acceptor energy levels in the energy band diagram of doped semiconductors.

topics.title: Formation of a p-n junction

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the roles of diffusion and drift in forming a p-n junction and reaching equilibrium.
Describe the depletion region, its immobile charges, its electric field and the barrier potential.

topics.title: Semiconductor diode under bias and its V-I characteristics

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how forward bias lowers the barrier and causes minority carrier injection and a large current.
Explain how reverse bias raises the barrier, widens the depletion region and gives a small saturation current.
Interpret the V-I characteristic of a diode, including cut-in voltage and dynamic resistance.

topics.title: Junction diode as a rectifier

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the working and output of a half-wave rectifier.
Explain how a centre-tap full-wave rectifier uses two diodes to rectify both half cycles.
Explain how a capacitor input filter smooths the pulsating output of a rectifier.
